Package com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.fluid

Class BBFluidLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.fluid.BBFluidLogic
public class BBFluidLogic extends Object
Coordinates finite Big and Huge Bucket world transactions after BBItem selects a player gesture. Capability transfer, world pickup, world placement, and native powder-snow placement remain owned by their shared primitives; this class applies finite-mode admission, protection, bucket debit or credit, and player observability around those operations.

    • tryTakeWithContext

      public boolean tryTakeWithContext(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.protection.ProtectionContext context)
      Tries to take one fluid unit using an explicit player or automation context.

      A sided block capability has priority and owns dispatch even when it refuses. Otherwise the world block's bucket-pickup contract is used. The exact target is protected before mutation. The server credits the finite bucket and emits the matching sound and fluid game event; player world pickup also awards the item-use statistic and filled-bucket criterion, while a capability pickup awards only the statistic. The client performs prediction without changing either state.

      Returns:
      true for an accepted client prediction or a completed server transaction; false leaves the world and bucket unchanged

    • tryPlace

      public boolean tryPlace(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.protection.ProtectionContext context, boolean allowFaceOffset)
      Tries to place one fluid unit using an explicit player or automation context.

      A sided block capability has priority. Otherwise placement uses vanilla-style world rules; allowFaceOffset permits a blocked clicked position to resolve to its neighbor along the hit face but does not bypass placement validity. Protection is checked at the actual target. A server success debits one finite unit, emits sound and a fluid-place game event, and awards the item-use statistic to a player. The client predicts without debit or world mutation.

      Returns:
      true for an accepted client prediction or a completed server transaction; false leaves the world and bucket unchanged

    • tryPlacePowder

      public boolean tryPlacePowder(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.protection.ProtectionContext context, boolean allowFaceOffset)
      Tries native powder-snow placement with explicit authorization identity.

      allowFaceOffset controls whether the native placement context may select the adjacent block; it does not relax native placement checks. The exact destination is protected before native placement. Player calls enter through ItemStack.useOn, so Forge owns snapshot capture, place-event cancellation, hand rollback, and player accounting. Automation calls use the same block-item placement without fabricating a player transaction.

      Returns:
      true for an accepted client prediction or a committed server placement; false leaves the block and bucket unchanged
